sources.title: Bernhard Keller, Introduction to A-infinity algebras and modules

contents.name: Definition of an uncurved A∞-algebra and the signed Stasheff identities
contents.argument: The source gives cohomological operations of degree 2−n, the all-arity Stasheff sum, the Koszul tensor rule and the warning that elementwise evaluation adds signs.

contents.name: The arity-one, arity-two and arity-three consequences of the A∞ identities
contents.argument: The source spells out square-zero m1, the signed derivation identity for m2 and the associator homotopy supplied by m3; the batch proves these by direct substitution into its fixed formula.

contents.name: A differential graded algebra as the strict A∞ case
contents.locator: §3.1, immediate consequences after the defining identities
contents.argument: When all operations above arity two vanish, the source identifies the remaining structure with a differential graded algebra; the local proposition verifies every arity directly from the DGA axioms.

contents.name: A∞-morphisms, their Taylor maps, and quasi-isomorphisms
contents.argument: The source gives Taylor-map degrees, the full morphism identity, and the criterion that the first component be a quasi-isomorphism; the batch fixes that exact sign formula locally.

contents.name: General minimal-model existence and uniqueness theorem
contents.argument: Keller states the general transfer theorem but explicitly notes that some results in these introductory notes are not proved there; this batch proves one finite example and does not use general transfer as a supplier.
contents.reason: The cited notes announce a general minimal-model theorem without supplying its full proof here; the assigned local example is constructed with an explicit A∞-quasi-isomorphism, and no general transfer theorem is claimed.

contents.name: The relation between a nonzero transferred m3 and a defined triple Massey product
contents.argument: Keller explains and illustrates the Massey-product role of m3; the batch checks a different finite DGA and its explicit minimal A∞-quasi-isomorphism rather than importing the source example.

contents.name: Koszul rule and graded tensor signs
contents.argument: The notes state the graded tensor convention used to evaluate the signed Stasheff identities; the local definition records the map-tensor rule and permutation sign explicitly.

contents.name: Triple Massey data and the ternary operation
contents.argument: The notes explain how null-homotopies for adjacent products produce a degree −1 Massey representative and how the ternary operation records the same obstruction; the pair fixes its own sign and proves closure.

contents.name: Closure of the triple Massey representative
contents.argument: The source motivates the representative, while the local lemma supplies the full signed Leibniz calculation needed to show it is a cocycle.

contents.name: Triple Massey product as a set over representative choices
contents.argument: The notes discuss the dependence on representatives and null-homotopies; the local definition forms the subset over all such valid choices and makes the empty case explicit.

sources.title: Jean-Louis Loday and Bruno Vallette, Algebraic Operads

contents.name: Independent A∞ definition and strict differential graded algebra example
contents.argument: The book encodes A∞ structures by square-zero coderivations and records the strict DGA special case in its chain convention; the local items retain Keller's unsuspended cohomological convention and prove it directly.

contents.name: L∞ identities in an operadic unsuspended convention
contents.argument: The book supplies a separate skew-operation convention; it is used as an independent treatment only, because no sign translation is made into the batch's owner-locked shifted coalgebra model.

contents.name: Coderivation formulation of A∞ and L∞ structures
contents.argument: The book identifies the A∞ and L∞ structures with square-zero coderivations on cofree tensor and symmetric coalgebras; the local proof supplies the full unshuffle and corestriction argument in its fixed cohomological signs.

contents.name: Nilpotent Maurer–Cartan gauge group and deformation functor
contents.argument: The source constructs gauge equivalence for nilpotent dg Lie algebras and uses a local Artin maximal ideal; this batch proves only filtered convergence and explicitly escalates the missing general gauge construction.
contents.reason: The displayed nilpotent dg Lie gauge action is not a general L∞ deformation classification; the assigned page would need its own filtered morphism, gauge relation and deformation-object proof before claiming a moduli correspondence.

contents.name: Koszul signs in graded tensor and symmetric constructions
contents.argument: The book fixes the graded tensor and permutation signs used in the operadic and coalgebra formulas; this pair records the exact convention as a prerequisite definition.

contents.name: Reduced symmetric coalgebra with the unshuffle coproduct
contents.argument: The book presents the reduced cofree cocommutative coalgebra and its unshuffle coproduct; the local item writes the quotient and signs explicitly.

contents.name: Coproduct laws and conilpotence of the graded shuffle coalgebra
contents.argument: The source uses the cofree symmetric coalgebra and unshuffle coproduct; the local proof checks descent, coassociativity, cocommutativity, conilpotence and primitives term by term.

contents.name: Cofree conilpotent cocommutative coalgebra universal property
contents.argument: The proposition identifies the cofree symmetric coalgebra model; the local proof gives the explicit finite Taylor formula and proves both the coalgebra identity and uniqueness.

contents.name: Coderivations from corestrictions to cogenerators
contents.argument: The book encodes infinity structures by coderivations on cofree coalgebras; the local lemma spells out the unshuffle extension formula and proves existence and uniqueness.

contents.name: Shifted coalgebra definition of L∞ structure
contents.argument: The source develops the L∞/sh-Lie coalgebra encoding; the local definition locks the shifted W=V[1] convention, degree-one coderivation, and absence of a curvature term.

contents.name: Square-zero coderivation and higher Jacobi identities
contents.argument: The book gives the square-zero coderivation characterization; the local proof identifies each cogenerator projection with the displayed shifted unshuffle Jacobi sum and proves the converse by conilpotent induction.

contents.name: Complete or nilpotent filtration and Maurer–Cartan equation
contents.argument: The source formulates Maurer–Cartan theory under nilpotence/filtration hypotheses; the local definition states the exact separated complete filtration and arity-additive compatibility conditions used here.

contents.name: Convergence of the filtered Maurer–Cartan series
contents.argument: The source treats Maurer–Cartan elements for nilpotent filtered structures; the local proof establishes convergence for the stated complete filtration by stabilization in every quotient.

contents.name: Definition of a filtered Maurer–Cartan element
contents.argument: The local definition specializes the source’s Maurer–Cartan equation to the completed shifted coalgebra model and cites the proved convergence result.

contents.name: Nilpotent dg Lie gauge action and deformation functor
contents.argument: The source constructs gauge equivalence in a nilpotent dg Lie setting with a local Artin maximal ideal; this is narrower than the assigned general filtered L∞ classification claim.
contents.reason: The cited construction is for nilpotent dg Lie algebras and a specified Artin base. Extending it to the assigned general filtered L∞ setting requires a separate filtered morphism, gauge relation, deformation object, and compatibility proof.

sources.title: Tom Lada and Jim Stasheff, Introduction to sh Lie algebras for physicists
sources.locator: The coderivation formulation and the sh Lie Structures section, PDF pp. 2–8

contents.name: The sh Lie operations and their degree- and sign-sensitive suspension convention
contents.argument: The source gives an unsuspended skew-bracket convention and then its explicit suspension formula; the batch records this as a convention comparison and makes no silent translation.
contents.reason: The assigned contract selects a different degree+1 coderivation on V[1]; reproducing or translating the source's unsuspended l_n signs is unnecessary and would add a separate proof obligation.

contents.name: Extension of the shifted operations to a coderivation by unshuffles
contents.argument: The source defines the coderivation extension by unshuffles; the batch gives its own complete well-definedness, coderivation and uniqueness proof in the locked degree+1 convention.

contents.name: Square-zero coderivation verification of the higher Jacobi identities
contents.argument: The source expands the square of the shifted coderivation into unshuffle terms and checks cancellations; the batch separately proves the projection-to-cogenerators equivalence with its explicit Koszul signs.

contents.name: Closed string field theory gauge transformations and N-point functions
contents.argument: These are physics applications with separate ghost-degree, pairing and action hypotheses and are not part of the assigned pure-mathematics A/B pair.
contents.reason: The assigned pages develop only algebraic A∞ and shifted L∞ structures; physical fields, actions and gauge transformations need extra data and are not used as mathematical premises here.

contents.name: Shifted coderivation extension by unshuffles
contents.argument: The source constructs the coderivation from shifted operations by unshuffles; the local lemma independently checks its quotient well-definedness, coderivation identity and uniqueness.

contents.name: Square-zero coderivation expansion into higher Jacobi identities
contents.argument: The source relates square-zero to the shifted Jacobi identities; the local lemma proves the corestriction formula and both implication directions with explicit Koszul signs.

canonical.name: minimal A∞-model
canonical.detail: A minimal model is defined as data with a quasi-isomorphism; no general existence or transfer theorem is asserted.

canonical.name: an associative algebra as an A∞-algebra
canonical.detail: The companion checks the strict associative special case directly from the A∞ identities.

canonical.name: a finite complete filtered L∞ Maurer–Cartan equation
canonical.detail: The companion computes a finite filtered Maurer–Cartan equation and its solutions.

canonical.name: without a complete filtration an infinite Maurer–Cartan sum may be undefined
canonical.detail: An explicit direct-sum example shows the unfiltered series need not define a vector.

canonical.name: the Maurer–Cartan equation alone does not specify gauge classes
canonical.detail: A zero L∞ structure has multiple possible equivalence relations on the same Maurer–Cartan set.

canonical.name: the general Maurer–Cartan deformation correspondence needs a proved gauge construction
canonical.detail: The general deformation-class correspondence remains a required owner decision because the batch does not define or prove filtered gauge equivalence.
canonical.reason: The assigned general deformation correspondence needs a separately specified deformation object, filtered morphism, gauge relation and proof that it matches deformation equivalence.
